route: Orders as certificates: the lattice of total preorders of the average values, the consistency operator on it (decode by the residue backward induction, then re-sort), the uniqueness of its fixed point, and the identification of the resulting lift with the antipodal walk on the profile cube.
object: The set of total preorders on the letters A = Vavg u {t0,t1} equipped with the CONSISTENCY OPERATOR Phi(<=) := ord(x_<= |_A), where x_<= is obtained by running the residue backward induction of def:residue with the ranks of <= as ordinal payoffs, letting sigma/tau take a successor attaining the max/min, and evaluating that profile exactly; a preorder is CONSISTENT when it is a fixed point.
headline: On a stopping SSG the consistent order is UNIQUE, so the order lattice carries a poly-time-checkable certificate with a unique accepting witness of O(b log b) bits naming no strategy (b = the average successors of controlled vertices, plus the sinks); but the lift that certificate suggests is not new and not an algorithm — it is the antipodal walk on the profile cube of def:profile-orientation, hence all-switches / the residue rule when one player is absent, it provably cannot cycle when |C| <= 2, and it cycles with period 3 on an explicit 23-vertex stopping game with |C| = 3.

results.name: ol:unique — the consistent order is unique
results.statement: Let G be a stopping SSG and A := Vavg u {t0,t1}. Decode a total preorder <= on A (rank 0 = top class) by (i) running the backward induction of def:residue over the acyclic subgraph induced on C (lem:trapchar) with the ordinal payoffs -rk on A, and letting sigma take at each Max vertex a successor attaining the maximum and tau at each Min vertex one attaining the minimum, ties broken arbitrarily; (ii) putting x_<= := v_{sigma,tau}, one exact linear solve. Call <= CONSISTENT if the preorder induced by x_<= on A is <= again. Then <= is consistent for one tie-breaking, equivalently for every tie-breaking, if and only if <= is the preorder induced by w*; and then x_<= = w* for every tie-breaking. Consequently orders are a sound and complete certificate system for SSG-Value with a polynomial-time verifier and a UNIQUE accepting witness of O((a+2)log(a+2)) bits that names no strategy.
results.why_not_implied: thm:order-determines asserts only that the TRUE preorder decodes to w*; it says nothing about false preorders, and soundness of the certificate is precisely the statement that no false preorder reproduces itself under its own decoding — which needs the identity x = D_x propagated along the acyclic controlled subgraph, not available in three lines from the decoding argument.
results.argument: Assume <= consistent with x := x_<=. Its classes are exactly the level sets of x|_A, so psi(r) := the common x-value of the letters of rank r is strictly decreasing and theta(-r) := psi(r) is a strictly increasing map from the ordinal payoffs used in the decode to the payoffs x|_A. Strictly increasing maps commute with max and min, so the decode's backward induction R and the residue D of def:residue run with payoffs x|_A satisfy D = theta o R on C; in particular sigma attains max(D(v0),D(v1)) at every Max vertex and tau the minimum at every Min vertex. Next, x = D on C, by induction along a topological order of the (acyclic, lem:trapchar) subgraph induced on C: G stopping gives x = T_{sigma,tau}x (thm:contraction), so x(v) = x(chosen successor), which equals D(chosen successor) — by definition of D if that successor lies in A, by the induction hypothesis otherwise — and the chosen successor attains the extremum defining D(v). Hence x = D everywhere, so at a Max vertex x(v) = max(x(v0),x(v1)) and at a Min vertex the minimum, while at average vertices and sinks x = v_{sigma,tau} already satisfies the equation: Tx = x, so x = w* by thm:contraction and <= is the true order. The converse and the tie-break independence are thm:order-determines.
results.verification: Exhaustive in exact rational arithmetic over EVERY total preorder on A and EVERY tie-breaking of the decode, with ground truth w* by enumeration of all positional pairs: 308 random stopping games with |A| <= 6 (n = 4..8, 0-2 Max, 0-2 Min; 75/541/4683 preorders each); 46 random stopping games with |A| = 7 (47293 preorders each); and, freshly generated and larger, 76 stopping games with n = 10..15, 1-3 Max, 1-3 Min, |A| = 6. In every one of these the only consistent preorder was the true one and its decode was exactly w*, for every tie-breaking. On the 23-vertex game OL3 (|A| = 22) 20000 random preorders were tested and none but the true one is consistent. The decoder was implemented twice — as the residue backward induction and as the iterated-attractor form printed in thm:order-determines — and the two agree, profile for profile and vector for vector, on 56 stopping games at every preorder on their letters. Files: ol.py, olns.py, t_unique.py, t_unique7.py, t_unique_big.py, t_cross.py; logs uniq1.log, uniq2.log, uniq7.log, uniqbig.log.

results.name: ol:read — only the read letters are needed, and they are already rigid
results.statement: Let B := {t0,t1} u {p in Vavg : p is a successor of some controlled vertex}. The decode of ol:unique consults <= only through <=|_B, and the unique total preorder on B whose decode induces it back on B is the one induced by w*. Hence SSG-Value has a unique polynomial-time-verifiable certificate of O(b log b) bits with b = |B| <= min(a+2, 2|C|+2), and O(b log b) adaptive SSG-Compare queries between average vertices suffice.
results.why_not_implied: thm:order-determines' count is O((a+2) log(a+2)) and involves no other parameter; the sharpening to the average successors of the controlled vertices (which can be O(1) while a = Theta(N), as on H_m where B = {c_1, h, t0, t1}) is a different bound, and its uniqueness half is ol:unique, not thm:order-determines.
results.argument: Every value D(v) produced by the backward induction at a controlled vertex is x(p) for some p in B (induction along the topological order: the extremum is attained at a successor, which is controlled and handled inductively, or lies in A and is then a successor of a controlled vertex, i.e. in B). So the decode reads only the order on B. Running the proof of ol:unique with B in place of A is unchanged: it derives x = D on C and then Tx = x.
results.verification: The B-restricted decode and consistency test were exercised as part of the exhaustive runs of ol:unique (the decode there literally never consults a letter outside B); on H_m (m = 3, 5) and on the wedge WD(4,2,6) the read set has 4 and 6 letters against a = 7, 11 and 16 average vertices. Files: ol.py (decode), t_cross.py.

results.name: ol:nonstopping — the stopping hypothesis is necessary
results.statement: Let NS be the SSG on non-sinks {v,p,q} with v in Vmax, p,q in Vavg, v -> (v,p), p -> (t1,q), q -> (v,t0). It is not stopping and val = (2/3, 2/3, 1/3). With the attractor form of the decoder of thm:order-determines (a controlled vertex attracted to no level set placed in t0's class) and the evaluation of thm:eval-stopfree, TWO distinct total preorders on A = {p,q,t0,t1} are consistent: t0 < q < p < t1, which decodes to val, and t0 ~ q < p < t1, which decodes to (0, 1/2, 0) =/= val. So without stopping the order certificate is neither unique nor sound.
results.why_not_implied: prop:bsi-nonstopping says the stopping hypothesis is needed for bidirectional improvement, a statement about a switching rule and its halting; it says nothing about the decodability or the uniqueness of an order certificate, and the failure here is located precisely where ol:unique's proof uses lem:trapchar (the controlled subgraph is no longer acyclic, so x = D_x fails).
results.argument: {v} is a trap so NS is not stopping; val is the least fixed point of T (thm:lfp-general), giving val(v) = val(p) = 2/3, val(q) = 1/3. For either preorder the Max attractor of {t1} misses v and that of {t1,p} contains it, so v lands in p's class and both of v's successors then carry that class: the tie-breaking is free. sigma(v) = p gives v_sigma = val, whose induced preorder is the first; sigma(v) = v makes {v} a trap, so v_sigma = (0,1/2,0) by thm:eval-stopfree, whose induced preorder is the second.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic; the enumeration of all 75 total preorders on A and both tie-breakings returns exactly these two consistent preorders and no others. A wider search over 3000 random non-stopping games with |A| <= 6 found no preorder other than the true one that is consistent under EVERY tie-breaking of its own decode, and never found the true preorder inconsistent under all of them — so the failure recorded here is exactly the tie-breaking freedom that acyclicity of C removes. Files: olns.py, t_ns.py, t_ns2.py.

results.name: ol:profile-walk — the order lift IS the antipodal walk on the profile cube (a proved collapse)
results.statement: Call G separated if every successor of a controlled vertex lies in A (lem:normalform makes every game separated). Let G be stopping, separated and profile-nondegenerate (def:profile-orientation), and let pi be a profile with value y_pi. Then the decode of ord(y_pi|_A) is the profile pi xor s_C(pi), so Phi(ord(y_pi|_A)) = ord(y_{pi xor s_C(pi)}|_A): on the orbit of any profile the order lift is exactly the antipodal walk of the profile orientation of def:profile-orientation, which switches at once every controlled vertex whose owner prefers its other action. In particular the order lift is the all-switches rule on a separated one-player game and a residue improvement step (def:residue-rule) on an arbitrary one-player game.
results.why_not_implied: def:profile-orientation defines an orientation of the profile cube and thm:profile-uso proves it is a USO; neither mentions the order lattice, the decode of thm:order-determines, or any dynamics on preorders. The identification is what transfers everything known about the profile cube to the order-lattice programme, and it is what shows the programme is not a new algorithm.
results.argument: Separatedness makes the backward induction of the decode have depth one: at a Max vertex it compares the ranks of two letters, which are ordered as their y_pi-values are, and y_pi(v) = y_pi(v^{pi(v)}); so the decode keeps pi(v) exactly when the other option evaluates lower at y_pi and switches exactly when it evaluates higher — which is the definition of s_C(pi) — and dually at Min; nondegeneracy excludes equality. For one player the decode is a Max strategy attaining max(D(v0),D(v1)) at every Max vertex, the only property of rho(sigma) used in the proof of thm:residue-correct(b),(c), so val_{sigma'} >= D >= val_sigma with equality only at an optimum.
results.verification: Checked profile by profile on the built game OL3 (23 non-sinks): the decoded profile equals pi xor s_C(pi) at all 8 profiles, with the out-sets recomputed from the game in exact arithmetic and matching thm:cyclic-uso's printed table. Checked on 1100 random separated stopping games with 1-3 Max and 1-3 Min: the decoded profile equals the antipodal step at every profile visited. Files: ol.py, cyc_build.py, cyc2_build.py, t_cyc.py, t_sep.py.

results.name: ol:small-C — with at most two controlled vertices the order lift cannot cycle
results.statement: Let G be stopping, separated and profile-nondegenerate with |C| <= 2. Then the order lift has no cycle of length greater than one; from every start it reaches the true order within four decodes, and four are attained.
results.why_not_implied: thm:cyclic-uso exhibits a directed 6-cycle of SINGLE improving switches on a 3-cube; it gives no lower bound on the number of controlled vertices needed for any cyclic behaviour, and it says nothing about the simultaneous (antipodal) walk, which converges from two of the eight profiles of its own instance. The threshold statement — no cycle at |C| <= 2 — is proved here from lem:profile-trichotomy plus the affine readouts, and it is what makes the cycle at |C| = 3 sharp.
results.argument: One player: the decoded vectors increase strictly until optimal (ol:profile-walk plus thm:residue-correct), so a cycle would make them constant. One Max vertex v and one Min vertex u: by ol:profile-walk the lift is pi -> pi xor s_C(pi) on four profiles, so a cycle has length 2, 3 or 4, and by lem:profile-trichotomy each of the four edges of the square carries a well-defined direction, so the lift is (i,j) -> (M(j), m(i)). Length 2: if the two profiles differ in one coordinate w the cycle asserts w in s_C(pi) and w in s_C(pi'), contradicting lem:profile-trichotomy; if in both, the four one-sided improving switches chain into y_00 <= y_10 <= y_11 <= y_01 <= y_00 with a strict inequality, absurd. Length 3: the three profiles form a path and either orientation forces one coordinate to be strictly switchable at both ends of one edge. Length 4: M and m are bijections with M o m the transposition, so after renaming v's actions the cycle is (0,0)->(1,0)->(1,1)->(0,1)->(0,0). Separatedness and first-passage decomposition of the average part (the affine readouts of def:profile-orientation) give profile-independent constants with (1-a_i)V_ij = b_i U_ij + c_i and a_i < 1 (a_i = 1 would make the play from v under action i return to v almost surely, giving a trap and contradicting lem:trapchar). The four preferences at v subtract, in pairs, to (1-a_0)dV > b_0 dU and (1-a_1)dV' > b_1 dU', where dV = V_10 - V_11, dU = U_10 - U_11, dV' = V_01 - V_00, dU' = U_01 - U_00, all >= 0 because the two Min steps of the cycle are improving switches; the profile identities give (1-a_1)dV = b_1 dU and (1-a_0)dV' = b_0 dU'. Cross-multiplying the first inequality by dU' against the second identity, and the second inequality by dU against the first identity, yields (1-a_0)(dV dU' - dV' dU) >= 0 strictly if dU' > 0 and (1-a_1)(dV' dU - dV dU') >= 0 strictly if dU > 0; since a_0, a_1 < 1 both differences vanish and dU = dU' = 0, whence dV = 0 from the identity and the inequality reads 0 > 0.
results.verification: Exhaustive over the reduced one-Max/one-Min family — the two Max options and the two Min options as affine substochastic readouts on the denominator-4 grid with leak at least 1/4, which is exactly what first-passage decomposition of any separated stopping game of this shape produces — 189225 nondegenerate systems, no cycle. 400 random separated stopping games with 1 Max and 1 Min and 400 with 2 Max, each run from the coarsest and 59 random preorders: every orbit has period 1, and the largest number of decodes before repetition observed is 4, so the bound is attained. 5000 random (not necessarily separated) 1-Max-1-Min stopping games with 40 random starts each: no cycle. 300 random separated 2-Max-1-Min games: also no cycle, so the |C| = 3 instance had to be engineered. Files: t_11.py, t_sep.py, hunt_cycle.py; logs g11.log, cyc3.log.

results.name: ol:lift-cycles — the order lift cycles with period three at |C| = 3
results.statement: Let OL3 be the stopping SSG on 23 non-sinks (2 Max vertices a,b, 1 Min vertex m, 20 average vertices, dyadic with denominator 16) obtained from the normal form of thm:cyclic-uso with the two actions of m exchanged, each option realised by the balanced binary tree of average vertices over its sixteen dyadic units; it is separated and profile-nondegenerate and w*(a,b,m) = (1/4, 15/64, 1/8). The order lift started from the COARSEST preorder enters, after one decode, a cycle of length three through the orders of the profile values (1/4,15/64,225/1024), (1/9,5/48,1/18), (1/4,1/8,1/8), pairwise distinct as preorders on the 22 letters. Hence the decode-and-re-sort fixed-point iteration on the order lattice, whose unique fixed point is the true order by ol:unique, is not an algorithm: it is a Tarski-style search whose operator is not monotone under any lattice order, and no sound lift can be built from it.
results.why_not_implied: thm:cyclic-uso proves a directed 6-cycle of single improving switches in the profile orientation and remarks, as an unchecked attribution to Condon, that simultaneous switching by both players need not converge; it exhibits no instance of a simultaneous-switch cycle, and a USO with a directed cycle may perfectly well have a converging antipodal walk — on this very instance two of the eight profiles converge. What is proved here is that the antipodal walk on the paper's instance closes into a triangle, that this triangle is what the order lattice's own iteration does, and that the instance is realised by a built and verified game rather than by a normal form.
results.argument: By ol:profile-walk the lift is the antipodal walk of the profile orientation. The out-sets printed in thm:cyclic-uso are {a,m}, {a,b}, {b,m} at the three profiles in question, and flipping each out-set in turn closes the triangle. Exchanging the two actions of m is a relabelling of the game that leaves the orientation unchanged up to that relabelling and moves the all-first-successor profile — the one the coarsest preorder decodes to, since it makes all residue values tied — onto the triangle.
results.verification: The game was built from the normal form by an explicit tree constructor and every number was recomputed FROM THE GAME in exact rational arithmetic: 23 non-sinks, stopping by the trap characterisation; all eight profile values reproduce thm:cyclic-uso's table exactly; all 24 vertex-coordinate comparisons are strict (profile-nondegenerate); w* by enumeration of all 8 positional pairs. The lift from the coarsest preorder has pre-period 1 and period 3; six of the eight profile orders and 1619 of 2000 random preorders lead into the cycle; the consistency defect (the number of ordered pairs of letters on which a preorder and its decoding disagree, whose unique zero is the true order by ol:unique) takes the values 44, 50, 52, 44, ... along the orbit, so the lift is not a descent for it either. Files: cyc_build.py, cyc2_build.py, t_cyc.py, t_cross.py; the game is written out as OL3.json (and the unrelabelled version as cyclic_game.json).

restatements.label: thm:residue-correct
restatements.note: On a one-player stopping game the order lift is a residue improvement step in the sense of def:residue-rule (the same rule up to the choice among successors attaining the residue maximum), hence its decoded vectors are nondecreasing and strictly increasing until optimal; the one-player half of the order-lattice programme is therefore the paper's residue rule and inherits its open round count.

restatements.label: prop:allsw-auso
restatements.note: On a SEPARATED one-player stopping game the order lift is literally the all-switches rule, so on that half the programme is the pivot itself.

restatements.label: thm:matching-barrier
restatements.note: Every sound lift on the order lattice whose derivations are radius-one clauses over a vertex and its two successors is a local matching calculus in the sense of def:lmc and therefore stalls on G_8; in particular the arithmetic-free 'attractor closure' lift (close a sound up-set under: a Max vertex with some successor in it, a Min or average vertex with both successors in it) is exactly the (up)/(down) fragment of def:simorder and is dominated by the simulation preorder.

restatements.label: thm:gap-equivalence
restatements.note: Since the refinement lattice of partial preorders on A has height O(a^2) and a total order decodes to w*, a polynomial-time sound lift that strictly refines every non-total sound partial preorder exists if and only if SSG-Value is in P; and any lift programme that reaches totality has in particular named the top average vertex, which is target-equivalent by thm:top. The order-lattice programme as a whole is therefore target-equivalent, and only the mechanism inside it can be new.

gap: GAP: for every stopping SSG with |Vmax| = |Vmin| = 1 that is NOT separated — i.e. in which one of the two controlled vertices is a successor of the other, so that the decode's residue induction has depth two — the order lift has no cycle of length greater than one (measured true on 5000 random such games from 40 random starts each, and on 189225 nondegenerate systems of the separated reduced family, but the affine-readout cross-multiplication of ol:small-C's proof is stated only for the separated case).
next_steps: 1. The one useful direction left inside this object is the RANGE, not the lattice: ol:unique makes the order a unique witness of O(b log b) bits, so the question 'is there a polynomial-time procedure producing ONE true strict comparison between two average vertices, given the free seeds Z_0, Z_1' is the first lift, and it is not obviously target-equivalent (thm:top is about naming the maximum, not about naming any true comparison); settling it either way would close or open the programme at its first step. 2. ol:small-C's proof is a two-variable cross-multiplication in the affine readouts; the natural attempt is |C| = 3 with one Min vertex, where the paper's instance shows it must fail — locating exactly which inequality of the proof the cyclic instance violates would say what a convergent order lift would have to add (the candidates are: solve the Min side exactly each round, which is the residue rule, or refuse to switch a coordinate whose readout gradient has mixed sign). 3. ol:profile-walk makes the profile cube's antipodal walk an object with an order-lattice reading: the round count of that walk on games where it does converge (it converged on every random separated game tried, and on G* in two decodes) is an open quantity with no lower bound in the paper, and a superpolynomial family for it would be a two-player analogue of the pivot. 4. ol:read's parameter b = |B| is a new structural parameter (the average successors of the controlled vertices); whether bounded b gives a polynomial class beyond the trivial 2^{O(b log b)} enumeration is untested.
prior_art: From memory, unchecked against the sources. (a) Gimbert and Horn's algorithm for games with few random vertices enumerates the orderings of the random vertices and rebuilds the value vector from each; the decode of ol:def-consistent is its reconstruction half, and the paper already attributes thm:order-determines to it. What ol:unique adds is that the reconstruction is injective on consistent orders. (b) That simultaneous switching by both players need not converge is in Condon's analysis of algorithms for simple stochastic games; the paper records this attribution inside thm:cyclic-uso. ol:lift-cycles supplies a built instance of the simultaneous-switch cycle and identifies the rule with the order lattice's own iteration. (c) Stickney and Watson's LCP/USO correspondence underlies the profile cube (rem:lcp, thm:profile-uso). (d) SSG-Value in UP n coUP is standard via uniqueness of the value vector (Condon's NP n coNP argument); rem:ol-up only sharpens the witness size. (e) The parity-game progress-measure/universal-tree template that motivated the route was rebuilt here from first principles and is not imported: the observation recorded is that its value-lattice analogue is value iteration (monotone, local, exponential range by thm:vi-lower and lem:denominator-sharp) and its order-lattice analogue has small height but admits no monotone lift beyond the one-player one.

\subsection{Orders as certificates: the consistent order is unique}
\label{ol:sec-consistent}

Throughout, $C:=\Vmax\cup\Vmin$ and $A:=\Vavg\cup\{t_0,t_1\}$, the
\emph{letters}.

\begin{definition}[The decode, and consistency]\label{ol:def-consistent}
Let $G$ be stopping and let $\preceq$ be a total preorder on $A$, given by
its rank function $\mathrm{rk}:A\to\{0,\dots,\ell\}$, rank $0$ being the
top class. The \emph{decode} of $\preceq$ is computed in two steps.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item By \Cref{lem:trapchar} the subgraph induced on $C$ is acyclic. Run the
  backward induction of \Cref{def:residue} with the ordinal payoffs
  $-\mathrm{rk}$ on $A$, obtaining $R(v)$ for every $v\in C$, and let
  $\sigma$ choose at each $v\in\Vmax$ a successor attaining
  $\max(R(v^{(0)}),R(v^{(1)}))$ and $\tau$ at each $v\in\Vmin$ one attaining
  the minimum, ties broken arbitrarily.
\item Put $x_{\preceq}:=v_{\sigma,\tau}$: one exact linear solve.
\end{enumerate}
$\preceq$ is \emph{consistent} if the total preorder induced by $x_\preceq$
on $A$ is $\preceq$ again. Both steps are polynomial, and the certificate
$\preceq$ names no strategy and carries $O(|A|\log|A|)$ bits.
\end{definition}

The decode is the decoder of \Cref{thm:order-determines} written out: on a
stopping game the Max attractor of a level set in the deterministic residue
is exactly that backward induction. (Both forms were implemented and agree
on $56$ random stopping games at every one of the $75$, $541$ or $4683$
total preorders on their letters.)

\begin{theorem}[The consistent order is unique]\label{ol:unique}
Let $G$ be a stopping SSG. A total preorder $\preceq$ on $A$ is consistent
--- for one tie-breaking in \Cref{ol:def-consistent}(i), equivalently for
every one --- if and only if $\preceq$ is the preorder induced by $w^\ast$
on $A$; and then $x_\preceq=w^\ast$ for every tie-breaking.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
That the true preorder is consistent, with $x_\preceq=w^\ast$ under every
tie-breaking, is \Cref{thm:order-determines}.

Conversely let $\preceq$ be consistent for some tie-breaking and write
$x:=x_{\preceq}$, so that $\preceq$ is the preorder induced by $x$ on $A$.
Then the classes of $\preceq$ are exactly the level sets of $x|_A$, so
$\psi(r):=$ the common value of $x$ on the letters of rank $r$ is a well
defined and strictly decreasing function of $r$, and
$\theta(-r):=\psi(r)$ is a strictly increasing map from the payoffs
$\{-\mathrm{rk}(p)\}$ used in \Cref{ol:def-consistent}(i) to the payoffs
$x|_A$. Let $D$ be the backward induction of \Cref{def:residue} run with
the payoffs $x|_A$. A strictly increasing map commutes with $\max$ and
$\min$, so $D=\theta\circ R$ on $C$; in particular the successor chosen at
$v\in\Vmax$ attains $\max(D(v^{(0)}),D(v^{(1)}))$ and the one chosen at
$v\in\Vmin$ attains the minimum.

Next, $x=D$ on $C$. Induct along a topological order of the acyclic
subgraph induced on $C$. Since $G$ is stopping, $x=v_{\sigma,\tau}$ is the
unique fixed point of $T_{\sigma,\tau}$ (\Cref{thm:contraction}), so
$x(v)=x(\sigma(v))$ at $v\in\Vmax$ and $x(v)=x(\tau(v))$ at $v\in\Vmin$.
If the chosen successor lies in $A$ then $x=D$ there by definition of $D$;
otherwise it lies earlier in the topological order and $x=D$ there by the
induction hypothesis. In both cases
$x(v)=D(\text{chosen successor})=D(v)$, the last equality because the
chosen successor attains the extremum defining $D(v)$.

Hence $x=D$ on all of $V$, and therefore at $v\in\Vmax$
\[
  x(v)=D(v)=\max\bigl(D(v^{(0)}),D(v^{(1)})\bigr)
       =\max\bigl(x(v^{(0)}),x(v^{(1)})\bigr)=(Tx)(v),
\]
and likewise at $v\in\Vmin$; at an average vertex and at the sinks
$x=v_{\sigma,\tau}$ already satisfies the defining equation of $T$. So
$Tx=x$, and $x=w^\ast$ by \Cref{thm:contraction}. Consequently $\preceq$,
being the preorder induced by $x$, is the true one; and then every
tie-breaking gives $w^\ast$ by \Cref{thm:order-determines}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Only the read letters are needed]\label{ol:read}
Let $B:=\{t_0,t_1\}\cup\{p\in\Vavg:\ p\ \text{is a successor of some vertex
of}\ C\}$. The decode of \Cref{ol:def-consistent} depends on $\preceq$ only
through $\preceq|_B$, and the unique total preorder on $B$ whose decode
induces it back on $B$ is the one induced by $w^\ast$. Hence
\textsc{SSG-Value} has a certificate of $O(b\log b)$ bits with
$b:=|B|\le\min(a+2,\,2|C|+2)$, verifiable in polynomial time, and unique.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Every value $D(v)$, $v\in C$, produced by the backward induction is a value
$x(p)$ with $p\in B$, by induction along the topological order; so only the
order of $\preceq$ on $B$ is consulted. With $B$ for $A$ throughout, the
proof of \Cref{ol:unique} is unchanged: it derives $x=D$ on $C$ and then
$Tx=x$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{ol:rem-up}
\Cref{ol:unique} makes the order a \emph{unique} witness: both the yes- and
the no-instances of \Cref{prob:main} have exactly one accepted certificate
of $O(b\log b)$ bits, which places \textsc{SSG-Value} in
$\mathrm{UP}\cap\mathrm{coUP}$ with a witness far smaller than the value
vector (whose entries need $\Theta(a)$ bits each by
\Cref{lem:denominator-sharp}). That the problem lies in
$\mathrm{UP}\cap\mathrm{coUP}$ is not new --- the value vector is itself a
unique witness (from memory, unchecked against the source: Condon's
$\mathrm{NP}\cap\mathrm{coNP}$ argument); what \Cref{ol:unique} adds is the
size, and that the small witness is unique too. No algorithm follows:
enumerating preorders costs $2^{\Theta(a\log a)}$, worse than
\Cref{thm:few-avg}.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Stopping is necessary]\label{ol:nonstopping}
Let $\mathrm{NS}$ be the SSG on non-sinks $\{v,p,q\}$ with $v\in\Vmax$,
$p,q\in\Vavg$, $v\to(v,p)$, $p\to(t_1,q)$, $q\to(v,t_0)$; it is not
stopping, and $\val=(\tfrac23,\tfrac23,\tfrac13)$. Decode a preorder by the
attractor form of \Cref{thm:order-determines} (a controlled vertex attracted
to no level set is placed in the class of $t_0$) and evaluate by
\Cref{thm:eval-stopfree}. Then two distinct total preorders on
$A=\{p,q,t_0,t_1\}$ are consistent:
$t_0\prec q\prec p\prec t_1$, which decodes to $\val$, and
$t_0\sim q\prec p\prec t_1$, which decodes to
$(0,\tfrac12,0)\ne\val$. Both consistencies use the tie-breaking freedom at
$v$, whose two successors are placed in the same class by every preorder.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$\{v\}$ is a trap, so $\mathrm{NS}$ is not stopping, and $\val$ is the
least fixed point of $T$ (\Cref{thm:lfp-general}): $\val(v)=\val(p)$,
$\val(p)=\tfrac12(1+\val(q))$, $\val(q)=\tfrac12\val(v)$ give
$\val(v)=\tfrac23$. For either preorder the attractor of $\{t_1\}$ misses
$v$ and the attractor of $\{t_1,p\}$ contains it, so $v$ lands in $p$'s
class, which both its successors then carry, and the tie-breaking is free.
Taking $\sigma(v)=p$ gives $v_{\sigma}=\val$, whose induced preorder is the
first; taking $\sigma(v)=v$ makes $\{v\}$ a trap, so
$v_\sigma=(0,\tfrac12,0)$ by \Cref{thm:eval-stopfree}, whose induced
preorder is the second. (Exact rational arithmetic; the enumeration of all
$75$ preorders and both tie-breakings returns exactly these two.)
\end{proof}

\subsection{The order lift, and what it really is}\label{ol:sec-lift}

\begin{definition}[The order lift]\label{ol:def-lift}
$\Phi(\preceq)$ is the total preorder induced by $x_\preceq$ on $A$. By
\Cref{ol:unique} its unique fixed point is the true order, so the order
lattice carries a fixed-point formulation of \Cref{prob:main} whose
solution is unique and whose fixed-point test is one linear solve. Call $G$
\emph{separated} if every successor of a controlled vertex lies in $A$;
\Cref{lem:normalform} makes every game separated at the cost of average
vertices.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[The lift is the antipodal walk on the profile cube]
\label{ol:profile-walk}
Let $G$ be stopping, separated and profile-nondegenerate
(\Cref{def:profile-orientation}), and let $\pi\in\{0,1\}^{C}$ be a profile
with value $y_\pi$. Then the decode of the preorder induced by $y_\pi$ on
$A$ is the profile $\pi\oplus s_C(\pi)$, so
\[
  \Phi\bigl(\mathrm{ord}(y_\pi|_A)\bigr)
   =\mathrm{ord}\bigl(y_{\pi\oplus s_C(\pi)}|_A\bigr):
\]
on the orbit of any profile the order lift is exactly the \emph{antipodal
walk} of the profile orientation of \Cref{def:profile-orientation}, which
switches at once every controlled vertex whose owner prefers its other
action. In particular, on a separated one-player stopping game the order
lift is the all-switches rule (\Cref{prop:allsw-auso}), and on an arbitrary
one-player stopping game it is a residue improvement step in the sense of
\Cref{def:residue-rule} --- the same rule up to the choice among successors
attaining the residue maximum --- hence monotone and convergent
(\Cref{thm:residue-correct}).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$G$ is separated, so the backward induction of \Cref{ol:def-consistent}(i)
has depth one: at $v\in\Vmax$ it compares the ranks of $v^{(0)},v^{(1)}\in
A$, which by hypothesis are ordered as $y_\pi(v^{(0)})$ and
$y_\pi(v^{(1)})$ are, and $y_\pi(v)=y_\pi(v^{(\pi(v))})$. So the decode
keeps $\pi(v)$ when $y_\pi(v^{(\overline{\pi(v)})})<y_\pi(v)$ and switches
when the inequality is reversed; nondegeneracy excludes equality. That is
precisely the definition of $s_C(\pi)$, and dually at $\Vmin$. For one
player: with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ the decode is a Max strategy $\sigma'$
attaining $\max(D(v^{(0)}),D(v^{(1)}))$ at every $v$, which is the only
property of $\rho(\sigma)$ used in the proof of
\Cref{thm:residue-correct}(b),(c); hence $\val_{\sigma'}\ge D\ge\val_\sigma$
with equality only at an optimum, and the decoded vectors increase strictly
until the lift is at its fixed point.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Two controlled vertices: the lift converges]\label{ol:small-C}
Let $G$ be stopping, separated and profile-nondegenerate with $|C|\le2$.
Then the order lift has no cycle of length greater than one; from every
start it reaches the true order within four decodes, and the bound is
attained.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If one player is absent the decoded vectors are monotone by
\Cref{ol:profile-walk}, and a cycle would make them constant, so there is
none. Let $\Vmax=\{v\}$, $\Vmin=\{u\}$, and write a profile as $(i,j)$,
$y_{ij}=(V_{ij},U_{ij})$ its value on $C$. By \Cref{ol:profile-walk} the
lift is $F(\pi)=\pi\oplus s_C(\pi)$ on the four profiles, so a cycle has
length $2$, $3$ or $4$. Throughout we use \Cref{lem:profile-trichotomy}:
for $\pi'=\pi\oplus e_w$ exactly one of $w\in s_C(\pi)$, $w\in s_C(\pi')$
holds (nondegeneracy excludes the flat case), and in the first case
$y_\pi\le y_{\pi'}$ with strict inequality at $w$ when $w\in\Vmax$,
$y_{\pi'}\le y_\pi$ strictly at $w$ when $w\in\Vmin$. Consequently each of
the four edges of the square carries a well-defined direction, and we may
write $M(j)$ for the head of the $v$-edge at level $j$ and $m(i)$ for the
head of the $u$-edge in column $i$; then $F(i,j)=(M(j),m(i))$.

\emph{Length two.} If the two profiles differ in one coordinate $w$, the
cycle asserts $w\in s_C(\pi)$ and $w\in s_C(\pi')$, contradicting
\Cref{lem:profile-trichotomy}. If they differ in both, say $\pi=(0,0)$ and
$\pi'=(1,1)$, then $v,u\in s_C(0,0)$ and $v,u\in s_C(1,1)$, whence
$y_{00}\le y_{10}$ strictly at $v$, $y_{01}\le y_{00}$ strictly at $u$,
$y_{11}\le y_{01}$ strictly at $v$ and $y_{10}\le y_{11}$ strictly at $u$:
the four vectors are equal, contradicting strictness.

\emph{Length three.} Three profiles of the square form a path; renaming the
two actions of $v$ and of $u$ we may take them to be $(0,0),(1,0),(1,1)$.
If the cycle is $(0,0)\to(1,0)\to(1,1)\to(0,0)$ then $u\in s_C(1,0)$ and
$u\in s_C(1,1)$; if it is $(0,0)\to(1,1)\to(1,0)\to(0,0)$ then
$v\in s_C(0,0)$ and $v\in s_C(1,0)$. Both contradict
\Cref{lem:profile-trichotomy}.

\emph{Length four.} Here all four profiles occur, $M$ and $m$ are
bijections and $M\circ m$ is the transposition; renaming the two actions of
$v$ we may take $M$ to be the transposition and $m$ the identity, so that
the cycle is $(0,0)\to(1,0)\to(1,1)\to(0,1)\to(0,0)$, one coordinate at a
time. Since $G$ is separated, first-passage decomposition of the average
part to $C\cup\{t_0,t_1\}$ --- the affine readouts of
\Cref{def:profile-orientation} --- gives profile-independent constants
$a_i,b_i,c_i\ge0$ and $d_j,e_j,g_j\ge0$ with $a_i+b_i+c_i\le1$,
$d_j+e_j+g_j\le1$, such that the value of $v$'s action $i$ at a profile
with value $(V,U)$ is $a_iV+b_iU+c_i$ and that of $u$'s action $j$ is
$d_jV+e_jU+g_j$. Moreover $a_i<1$: $a_i=1$ would force $b_i=c_i=0$ and make
the play from $v$ under $\pi(v)=i$ return to $v$ almost surely, so the
vertices it meets form a trap and $G$ is not stopping
(\Cref{lem:trapchar}). The profile identities read
$(1-a_i)V_{ij}=b_iU_{ij}+c_i$. The four preferences at $v$ along the cycle
are $v\in s_C(0,0)$, $v\notin s_C(1,0)$, $v\in s_C(1,1)$,
$v\notin s_C(0,1)$, i.e.
\[
  (1-a_1)V_{00}<b_1U_{00}+c_1,\ \ (1-a_0)V_{10}>b_0U_{10}+c_0,\ \
  (1-a_0)V_{11}<b_0U_{11}+c_0,\ \ (1-a_1)V_{01}>b_1U_{01}+c_1 .
\]
Put $\Delta V:=V_{10}-V_{11}$, $\Delta U:=U_{10}-U_{11}$,
$\Delta V':=V_{01}-V_{00}$, $\Delta U':=U_{01}-U_{00}$; the steps
$(1,0)\to(1,1)$ and $(0,1)\to(0,0)$ are improving switches of $u$, so
$y_{11}\le y_{10}$, $y_{00}\le y_{01}$ and all four are $\ge0$.
Subtracting the second and third inequalities, and the fourth and first,
\[
  (1-a_0)\Delta V>b_0\Delta U,\qquad (1-a_1)\Delta V'>b_1\Delta U',
\]
while the identities give
$(1-a_1)\Delta V=b_1\Delta U$ and $(1-a_0)\Delta V'=b_0\Delta U'$.
Multiplying the first inequality by $\Delta U'\ge0$ and the second identity
by $\Delta U\ge0$ and subtracting gives
$(1-a_0)(\Delta V\Delta U'-\Delta V'\Delta U)\ge0$, strictly if
$\Delta U'>0$; multiplying the second inequality by $\Delta U$ and the
first identity by $\Delta U'$ and subtracting gives
$(1-a_1)(\Delta V'\Delta U-\Delta V\Delta U')\ge0$, strictly if
$\Delta U>0$. As $a_0,a_1<1$ the two force $\Delta U=\Delta U'=0$; then
$(1-a_1)\Delta V=b_1\Delta U=0$ gives $\Delta V=0$ and
$(1-a_0)\Delta V>b_0\Delta U$ reads $0>0$.

An orbit of a map without cycles on four points reaches its fixed point in
at most three steps, so at most four decodes are performed; four occur on
random instances.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Three controlled vertices: the lift cycles]
\label{ol:lift-cycles}
Let $\mathrm{OL}_3$ be the stopping SSG on $23$ non-sinks --- two Max
vertices $a,b$, one Min vertex $m$ and twenty average vertices --- obtained
from the normal form of \Cref{thm:cyclic-uso} with the two actions of $m$
exchanged, each option realised by the balanced binary tree of average
vertices over its sixteen dyadic units. It is separated and
profile-nondegenerate, $w^\ast(a,b,m)=(\tfrac14,\tfrac{15}{64},\tfrac18)$,
and the order lift started from the coarsest preorder enters, after one
decode, the cycle of length three
\[
  \mathrm{ord}\,y_{(0,0,0)}\ \to\ \mathrm{ord}\,y_{(1,0,1)}\ \to\
  \mathrm{ord}\,y_{(0,1,1)}\ \to\ \mathrm{ord}\,y_{(0,0,0)},
\]
whose profiles carry $(a,b,m)$-values
$(\tfrac14,\tfrac{15}{64},\tfrac{225}{1024})$,
$(\tfrac19,\tfrac5{48},\tfrac1{18})$ and $(\tfrac14,\tfrac18,\tfrac18)$,
pairwise distinct as preorders on the letters. Six of the eight profile
orders, and $1619$ of $2000$ random preorders, lead into it. So the order
lift, unlike the residue rule it restricts to on one player, is not an
algorithm.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The game was built from the normal form and all eight profile values
recomputed from the game in exact rational arithmetic, reproducing the table
of \Cref{thm:cyclic-uso}; all $24$ vertex--coordinate comparisons are
strict, so the game is profile-nondegenerate, and every option is a tree of
average vertices, so it is separated. By \Cref{ol:profile-walk} the lift is
the antipodal walk of the profile orientation, and the out-sets printed in
\Cref{thm:cyclic-uso} are $\{a,m\},\{a,b\},\{b,m\}$ at the three profiles
above (in the exchanged labelling), so the antipodal walk closes into the
displayed triangle. The coarsest preorder decodes to the
all-first-successor profile, which the exchange of $m$'s actions places on
the triangle.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{ol:rem-where}
The three statements bracket the order lattice exactly. \Cref{ol:unique}
says the lattice carries a genuine certificate: a polynomial-time test with
a unique accepting witness of $O(b\log b)$ bits that names no strategy.
\Cref{ol:profile-walk} says the one iteration the certificate itself
suggests --- decode, then re-sort --- is not new: it is the antipodal walk
on the profile cube of \Cref{def:profile-orientation}, hence the residue
rule of \Cref{def:residue-rule} when one player is absent and the
all-switches rule when moreover the game is separated. So on one player the
order-lattice programme is exactly the pivot of this paper and inherits its
open question, while with two players it fails outright at $|C|=3$ by
\Cref{ol:lift-cycles} and cannot fail below it by \Cref{ol:small-C}. What
breaks is the analogue of the parity-game lifting: on the value lattice the
lift $x\mapsto\max(x,Tx)$ is monotone, local and convergent but has
exponential range (\Cref{thm:vi-lower,lem:denominator-sharp}); on the order
lattice the range is a lattice of height $O(a^{2})$ but the only monotone
lift available is the one-player one. The comparison with the mechanisms of
\Cref{sec:gap} is one-sided for the same reason: every family recorded
there as a stall --- $G_8$, $S$, $H_m$, the wedge $\mathrm{WD}(e,j,m)$,
$\mathrm{CV}(e,s)$ --- has at most one Max vertex or no Min vertex at all,
so the order lift converges on each of them (measured: from the coarsest
preorder and from $200$ random preorders on $G_8$, $S$, $H_3$, $H_5$,
$\mathrm{WD}(4,2,6)$ and on $G^{\ast}$, whose seven controlled vertices it
settles in two decodes), and its own failure needs two players and three
controlled vertices. The defect
$d(\preceq):=\#\{(p,q)\in A^2:\ \preceq\ \text{and}\
\mathrm{ord}(x_\preceq)\ \text{disagree}\}$, whose unique zero is the true
order by \Cref{ol:unique}, is not decreased by the lift either: along the
cycle of $\mathrm{OL}_3$ it takes the values $44,50,52,44,\dots$
\end{remark}
